name: case-store

scripts.codegen: npx prisma generate --schema=apps/store-api/prisma/schema.prisma && npm run generate:api
scripts.build: npm run build -w apps/store-api -w apps/store-client -w apps/store-admin
scripts.lint: npm run lint -w apps/store-api -w apps/store-client -w apps/store-admin
scripts.test: npm run test -w apps/store-api -w apps/store-client -w apps/store-admin
scripts.typecheck: npm run typecheck -w apps/store-api -w apps/store-client -w apps/store-admin

//optionalDependencies: TASK-326. These are NOT dependencies of any app — they are the Linux native
addons of lightningcss and @tailwindcss/oxide, pinned here so they survive in
package-lock.json no matter which OS ran `npm install`.
WHY: both packages ship their addon as per-platform optional packages and pick
one at require() time. npm records only the ones installable on the resolving
machine. This lockfile is maintained on Windows, so it held only the
*-win32-x64-msvc entries; `npm ci` on ubuntu (which installs exactly what the
lockfile lists) then installed no addon at all and `next build` died with
'Cannot find module ../lightningcss.linux-x64-gnu.node'. Both frontend images
failed to build.
optionalDependencies, NOT devDependencies: a devDependency whose `os` field
excludes the host aborts `npm install` on Windows with EBADPLATFORM. Optional
deps are allowed to be uninstallable and are simply skipped.
VERSIONS MUST EQUAL THE PARENT'S EXACTLY (lightningcss@1.32.0,
@tailwindcss/oxide@4.3.3) — the addon is version-locked to its parent. When you
bump Tailwind or lightningcss, bump these in the same commit.
`scripts/check-lockfile-platforms.js` (CI job `lockfile-platform`) enforces both
the presence and the version match, because the one-off lockfile edit is not
durable: the next `npm install` on Windows would otherwise prune it silently.
LIMITATION — only linux-x64-gnu is covered. NOT musl (alpine) and NOT arm64.
An ARM server (Hetzner CAX / Ampere, Apple Silicon) fails exactly the same way.
Deploy targets must stay x86-64 glibc until these are pinned too; the frontend
images use node:22-slim (Debian/glibc) for this reason. See docs/deploy/05-first-deploy.md.
//overrides: TASK-343. Transitive advisories that the direct bump does NOT reach, because
the parent pins an exact version. Re-check on every `next` bump — drop an
entry the moment the parent ships a fixed version itself.
postcss: `next@16.2.12` declares `postcss: '8.4.31'` EXACTLY, so bumping next
does not clear GHSA-qx2v-qp2m-jg93 / GHSA-6g55-p6wh-862q / GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849
(fixed in 8.5.18). The runtime-reachable copy is store-api's: sanitize-html
runs postcss over style attributes of admin-authored rich text, so the
sourceMappingURL path-traversal is not merely a build-time concern.
sharp: `next` lists `sharp: '^0.34.5'` as an optional dependency, which
excludes the fix for the inherited libvips CVEs (0.35.3, semver-major). Without
the override, store-api gets 0.35.3 while next keeps a nested vulnerable 0.34.x
for its Image Optimization API — the copy that actually decodes remote images.
js-yaml (TASK-304): `@nestjs/swagger@11.4.6` declares `js-yaml: '5.2.1'`
EXACTLY, and 5.2.1 carries GHSA (exponential parsing time in flow
collections), fixed in 5.2.2. Note this is a DIFFERENT advisory from the
4.x prototype-pollution one that the swagger 7 -> 11 upgrade did clear; npm
reports the only 'fix' as downgrading swagger to 11.4.5, which is wrong.
NOTE ON APPLYING THESE: npm only evaluates `overrides` while building a fresh
ideal tree. Editing this block and re-running `npm install` over an existing
node_modules silently changes nothing — the entries land only after a clean
resolve (delete node_modules + package-lock.json, then install). The lockfile
in git already has them baked in, so `npm ci` reproduces them correctly.
Scoped per-parent rather than global on purpose: a bare top-level `sharp`
entry collides with store-api's own direct dependency on sharp, and npm then
ignores the override instead of erroring.
